title: Most balconies are bought and never sat on.
subtitle: The question is not whether a veranda is nice. It is whether this itinerary lets you use one.

text: A veranda is time, not square footage.
sub: You are buying hours spent sitting outside your own cabin. On a port-intensive summer itinerary you are ashore for most of them, and asleep for the rest.

items.head: How many sea days are there?
items.body: Fewer than two on a week-long sailing and the veranda is decoration you paid a premium for.

items.head: What is the month?
items.body: A Baltic balcony in October is a cold shelf behind glass. In June it is the best room you have.

items.head: Which side, and which way?
items.body: Scenic passages happen on one side. Knowing which is half the value of the position.

items.head: Is it overhung or overlooked?
items.body: A deck cantilevered above you takes the sky, the light and most of the point.

quote: I have moved more clients out of balconies than into them, and none of them have missed it.

text: Count your sea days. Then decide about the door.
sub: Two or more, in a warm month, and the veranda is the best value on the ship. Otherwise take a quiet midship ocean view and spend the difference on a guide who knows the town.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with.
body: Or send me the itinerary you're weighing up. I'll tell you plainly whether the balcony is worth it on that route, or whether it isn't.
